full_judgment: 24. The adaptation and fostering of Equity Jurisdiction in this Sub-Continent has been the concomitant effect of bringing on this soil the stream of administration of law from the fountainhead of English Jurisprudence. The remedy of injunction was undoubtedly borrowed by Courts of Chancery from the "Interdict" of Roman Law. "Interdicts" consisted of certain forms of words by which the "Praetor" either commanded or prohibited something to be done. In granting injunction Courts of this Sub-Continent were guided by Chancery practice in England. In this land in Criminal matters sections 133, 142 and 144 of The Code of Criminal Procedure deal with grant of injunction. In Civil matters law relating to grant of injunction is contained in The Code of Civil Procedure and Specific Relief Act which supplements The Code and occupies a middle ground between substantive law on the one hand and procedure on the other.
